translation_notes: Both queries use property-path alternatives (`rdfs:subClassOf|owl:equivalentClass`, `owl:allValuesFrom|owl:someValuesFrom|owl:hasValue`), and the first has three OPTIONALs: not BGPs, so `s{ }(self.onto_graph)`. The first query's prefixes (rdfs:, owl:), which the original relied on rdflib's default bindings for, are declared with @prefix.

Second query: the initBindings {'c': c, 'p': p} target variables that are NOT projected (SELECT ?r), so they become term interpolations in subject/object position, `{c} rdfs:subClassOf|... ; owl:onProperty {p} ;`: the initBindings dict disappears. This is the clean case of the bind_initbindings row.
Truthiness of the OPTIONAL columns is kept as Python (`if min_:`): a Literal 0 is falsy, so minCardinality 0 writes no sh:minCount, on both sides (the fixture has that case).

Context shim (shim.py): kgtk node classes (verbatim, except BNode() draws its id from a counter instead of uuid4 so two runs mint the same ids), Subject (without reify), Graph (reduced to add_subject/URI resolution), and SHACLOntoConverter minus the region and its sibling conversions. kgtk is not installed in the study venv.

Driver: `self` is a fresh converter whose onto_graph is the fixture; what is compared is the mutated `self` (the derived SHACL graph, by isomorphism, and the class-node table). Fixture: exact cardinality, falsy min 0 with a max, two ranges on one restriction (sh:or), equivalentClass + hasValue, the same property with another range on another class (ranges looked up per class and property), a restriction without range, and decoys (onProperty without owl:Restriction, an orphan restriction, a bare cardinality on a class); plus an ontology with no restriction. Mutant `{c}` -> `?c` in query 2 makes the check fail.
Not exercised: a blank-node class in `{c}` (ldpy's handling of an interpolated BNode in s{ } was not tried; the ids differ between sides in any case).
optimization_notes: optimized.py: the three `if exact/min_/max_:` blocks become one loop over (predicate, value) pairs with the same truthiness test and the same call order; the ranges list is a comprehension passed directly to `_build_property_ranges` (computed after the cardinalities, as before).

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: query 1 stays `s{ }` (three OPTIONAL); query 2, kept in `s{ }` by the translation for its two alternations, is now `m{ {c} {rdfs:subClassOf | owl:equivalentClass} [ a owl:Restriction ; owl:onProperty {p} ; {owl:allValuesFrom | owl:someValuesFrom | owl:hasValue} ?r ] }` read with `list()`: rdflib AlternativePaths in predicate position, the blank node keeps ?res unprojected so the solutions are bare terms with the SELECT's multiplicity. The rest is identical line for line.

No exception to the symmetry. A property path and a blank node `[ ... ]` in m{ } are not in the closed construction vocabulary. The notation loses on tokens: the SPARQL texts are single string tokens in Python.
